justification: Hillshade relief diagram for the brief's terrain card. Renders a coloured shaded-relief PNG from the DEM the terrain pipeline already loads (services/terrain_analysis._run_terrain_chain reads dem_arr), returns it as a base64 data URI on the existing satellite.terrain section, and TerrainCard shows it. Pure presentation — no new data source, no DB, no extra fetch.

pre_impl.existing_data: _run_terrain_chain already reads the DEM into dem_arr (float64, NaN at nodata) at terrain_analysis.py:895; the hillshade is rendered from that same array — no second fetch. Viz deps already in requirements (numpy, matplotlib==3.10.5, pillow==11.3.0).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The terrain section carried only numbers; the DEM that produced them was discarded. The fix surfaces the DEM itself as an indicative relief image. No assumption about regulatory values — relief is a picture, not a control.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: prior-art-checked: no existing hillshade/LightSource/shaded-relief renderer in services/ (grep = none). New helper _render_hillshade_png reuses the in-memory DEM via matplotlib.colors.LightSource.shade — no figure/Agg backend, no whitebox call, no fetch. Field flows through the existing _build_terrain_detail model_fields filter once added to the TerrainAnalysisDetail model.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No external call is added. The entire render is wrapped in try/except returning None; the terrain metrics dict is built independently, so a render failure leaves the numbers and the card intact (the image block is simply omitted).
pre_impl.frontend_type: Frontend reads hillshade_png_b64?: string|null off the terrain payload and renders a plain data URI guarded by truthiness; falls back to no image. tsc --noEmit passes.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: terrain was numbers only. After: a shaded-relief picture of the land (lighter = higher, shadows = slope) above the compass + summary. If the DEM is missing/flat/all-nodata, no image renders and the rest of the card is unchanged.

functions.name: _render_hillshade_png
functions.input: a 2-D DEM elevation array (float, NaN at nodata) and an optional max pixel edge
functions.output: a data:image/png;base64 URI of a coloured shaded relief (nodata transparent, downsampled to <=256px, capped at 400k chars), or None
functions.if_none: returns None on any failure (bad/None/1-D input, <16 finite cells, missing matplotlib/PIL, oversize) so the terrain metrics are never affected

values: N/A - no regulatory values. The image is a qualitative relief of the same DEM the metrics come from; vert_exag is a presentation choice and the caption marks it Indicative. Nothing regulatory is hardcoded.
queries: N/A - no new database or API query. Reuses dem_arr already loaded by _run_terrain_chain.

break_it.scenario: matplotlib or PIL is not installed in the runtime image
break_it.what_happens: an unguarded import would raise inside terrain analysis and could drop the whole terrain section
break_it.repro: the imports are inside the try block; ImportError is caught and the function returns None
break_it.how: render returns None; the metrics dict is assembled separately so terrain numbers still stream; the image block is omitted

break_it.scenario: The DEM is entirely nodata (NaN) or has fewer than 16 finite cells
break_it.what_happens: nanmin/nanmax over all-NaN warns and the shader could emit a garbage or blank image
break_it.repro: finite.sum() < 16 returns None before any shading; verified by test_all_nodata_returns_none
break_it.how: early return None; no image rendered

break_it.scenario: A perfectly flat DEM where vmax == vmin
break_it.what_happens: Normalize(vmin, vmax) with equal bounds divides by zero
break_it.repro: norm uses vmax if vmax > vmin else vmin + 1.0; test_flat_dem_does_not_crash asserts no raise
break_it.how: the degenerate range is widened by 1 m so Normalize is valid; output is a flat tint or None, never a crash

break_it.scenario: A non-array or 1-D value is passed (upstream shape change)
break_it.what_happens: indexing/shading on the wrong shape could raise
break_it.repro: np.asarray(...).ndim != 2 returns None; covered by test_none_input, test_non_array_input, test_one_dimensional_input
break_it.how: shape guard returns None before any rendering

break_it.scenario: A huge DEM produces an oversized data URI that bloats the brief stream
break_it.what_happens: a multi-MB base64 string could slow or break the SSE payload
break_it.repro: the DEM is downsampled to <=256px and the b64 is rejected (None) if it exceeds 400k chars; a realistic 200x200 DEM measured ~31 KB
break_it.how: downsample + length cap keep the inline image small; otherwise None

post_merge.other_repo: N/A - the brief backend runs on Railway (nswcompliance); this needs a backend redeploy to take effect, like ANEF. The frontend image rendering deploys via Vercel.
post_merge.manual_verify: After the nswcompliance redeploy, run a brief with satellite analysis on for a Sydney address: the Terrain card should show a shaded-relief image above the compass + summary. For an address where terrain fails or wasn't run, the card shows no image and the rest is unchanged.
